observation: Architecture critique round 1 (7/10 PASS) caught 2 CRITICALs + 3 WARNINGs with high precision; designer revised plan (3fc463a9) and builder executed revised plan cleanly in green phase with 5 impl commits before visual proof. Critique-then-revise loop is working; cost signal 1 round.

Code review round 1 found 2 blocking issues (F1 lint-red 15 errors + C1 WorkTeam bet chip omitted label → HEALTHY not ACTIVE) not caught in green phase. Builder executed diff but lint output diverged and one surface (WorkTeam) outside diff scope was missed. Cost: 1 extra review round + 2 fix commits (format + WorkTeam label). Lint should have been pre-submit gate.

Plan reconciliation table (5 spec⇆reality drifts enumerated, decisions 1a-7 load-bearing for casing contract / label vocab / AC1b BetCard visual parity gate) prevented zero mid-stream scope surprises. Builder had clear, documented decisions before writing code. AC4 lint rule motivation + AC2 exhaustiveness via Record<Enum,string> strategy was locked upfront.

AC1a TaskSheet scope boundary (dot-only, no TaskState chip, documented in plan + proof/README.md) challenged by code reviewer as 'missing proof' but was actually a deliberate scope decision approved in Phase 2. Boundary is sound, documented, satisfied. Reflects tension between 'comprehensive proof' and 'plan-scoped surfaces' — the spec's three-surface scenario conflated TaskState and session-status axes, which TaskSheet doesn't separate. No actual coverage gap.

Visual parity gate (Decision 5, BetCard ≤5% via `npm run ds:sync`) could not be independently verified due to port conflict (concurrent worktree vite on :5173). Reviewer accepted claim based on protected-test green + fresh proof image. Gate intent (pixel parity validation) deferred to builder's claim, not objective measurement. Matches CC-014 residual: Playwright proves e2e DOM, but visual tool (`ds:sync`) still relies on claim.

Cost signal: architecture critique (8 fig) + design-it-twice (Decision 1 casing contract) + plan revision (2h) = upfront investment before code. Critique led builder to skip Option A (presentation-status only), avoiding a regression in domain-information expressivity and protected-test breakage. Process discipline (CC-024 revision loop + CC-010 TDD) produced clean first-pass green (5 impl commits before proof). Subsequent round 1 code review found lint + WorkTeam scope, both preventable by pre-submit checklist (CC-011).

Lore capture and @lore AF12 decision honored: LiveDot promoted to design-system; local copies in WorkTask/TaskSheet deleted; design-system story + HTML dual-rep added; all three consumers (WorkBet, WorkTask, TaskSheet) now use promoted component. Zero dead code, clean refactoring.

TDD red-phase caught AC scope precisely: 6 failing test files (status-mapping, status-labels, knowledge-status-label, LiveDot, StatusChip-label, protected BetCard) before green phase. All tests green first run after implementation. Red phase forced specificity on casing contract, exhaustiveness guards, and three-surface parity proof.

ESLint rule design (AC4 no-local-status-builder) initially registered as 'warn', promoted to 'error' in Phase 4 fix. Plan said 'CI fails if fork reintroduced' — 'warn' does not enforce. Promotion was correct; rule now genuinely gates the constraint. Negative cases (shared *_LABEL not flagged, panelClass not flagged) covered. Lint extension pattern (custom rule + RuleTester) is solid, scalable.
